body:
Wire `.mch` URDF machine models into `camcraft-simview` (`camcraft-sim` checks and playback) and record the #2593 decisions.

## Context
Research in #2593 defined the URDF file contract across `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-geometry`, and `camcraft-sim`. `camcraft-simview` (#2586) owns the mapping from `camcraft_post::machine::MachineTree` into `camcraft_sim::machine_model` so `camcraft-sim` keeps no edge to `camcraft-post`.

## Scope
- In `crates/simview`, when `MachineTree::urdf` is present, resolve `urdf.file` relative to the `.mch` file directory and build the `MachineModel` through `camcraft_sim::machine_model` instead of generating loose blocks (#2584).
- When `MachineTree::urdf` is absent, keep the existing `.mch` model path (#2584, #2591).
- Feed posed URDF bodies into the machine-part collision check and playback renderer. Do not label URDF findings or passes as "judged on a generated model".
- Keep `.mch` `travel` authoritative in `MachineCheck`, print any URDF vs `.mch` limit discrepancy notes, and report a URDF mechanical joint limit overrun as a failed check (exit 2, with NC line number).
- Refuse a missing, unreadable, or invalid URDF or mesh with exit 1 and the named diagnostic; never fall back silently to a generated model.
- Add `docs/decisions/2593-urdf-machine-model.md` recording the research decisions of #2593 (`.mch` key and joint map, SI unit conversion, root frame, `.mch`-wins limit law, STL/OBJ scope, pure-Rust XML reader, and dropped options).

## Done means
Tests in `crates/simview/tests/` pin `camcraft-sim check` on a 3-axis NC program with a `.mch` referencing a URDF + binary STL fixture: a machine-part collision fails with exit 2 without the generated-model tag, a mechanical joint limit overrun fails with exit 2, a missing URDF or mesh refuses with exit 1, and a `.mch` without `urdf` still uses the generated model. `docs/decisions/2593-urdf-machine-model.md` exists.

Depends on #2586, #3638, and #3640.

Part of #2593
